title: EN 301 489-19 Testing for GNSS Devices
description: EN 301 489-19 V2.2.1 EMC testing services for GNSS receivers. Complete compliance support for CE marking under the Radio Equipment Directive.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: EN 301 489-19 V2.2.1 testing applies to Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receivers operating under the Radio Equipment Directive (RED). This standard defines electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) requirements specifically for equipment such as GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, and BeiDou receivers.
At ITC India, we conduct EN 301 489-19 V2.2.1 testing to ensure your GNSS-enabled devices meet European compliance requirements before CE marking.
For general EMC framework requirements, this standard must be read together with 👉 EN 301 489-1 (EMC common requirements for radio equipment).

sections.heading: What is EN 301 489-19?
paragraphs: EN 301 489-19 is a product-specific EMC standard developed by 👉 European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI).

sections.heading: The standard ensures that GNSS equipment
bullets: Does not generate excessive electromagnetic disturbances
Remains immune to external electromagnetic interference

sections.heading: Why EN 301 489-19 Testing is Important
paragraphs: GNSS receivers operate with very weak satellite signals. Even small electromagnetic disturbances can affect positioning accuracy.

sections.heading: Therefore, compliance ensures
bullets: Market access in the European Union
Smooth CE certification under the Radio Equipment Directive

sections.heading: Key Test Requirements Under EN 301 489-19 V2.2.1
paragraphs: Testing is performed along with EN 301 489-1 requirements.

sections.heading: Immunity Tests

sections.heading: External Reference
paragraphs: For official standard details, refer to: European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI) https://www.etsi.org

sections.heading: 1. Is EN 301 489-19 mandatory for CE marking?
paragraphs: Yes. GNSS radio receivers placed in the EU market must comply with this standard under the Radio Equipment Directive.

sections.heading: 2. Is EN 301 489-1 also required?
paragraphs: Yes. EN 301 489-19 must be read together with EN 301 489-1.

sections.heading: 3. Does this testing include radio performance testing?
paragraphs: No. EMC testing evaluates electromagnetic compatibility. Separate radio performance standards may apply.

sections.heading: 4. How long does testing take?
paragraphs: Typically 5–7 working days depending on product complexity.

sections.heading: 5. Can integrated GNSS modules be tested?
paragraphs: Yes. Both standalone and integrated modules can be tested.
